official_measurement_examples.name: Register duty
official_measurement_examples.fact: Relevant authorities must keep and publicise a register of individuals and associations seeking serviced plots for self-build or custom housebuilding.

official_measurement_examples.name: Serviced-plot definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: The statutory framework links a serviced plot to highway access and electricity, water and wastewater connections, including circumstances where those can be provided within the life of a development permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Three-year compliance period
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Time for Compliance and Fees Regulations set a three-year period after each base period for the authority's permission duty.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2023 Act counting rule
official_measurement_examples.fact: Levelling-up and Regeneration Act amendments require permissions counted toward the statutory duty to be specifically for self-build and custom housebuilding and provide for unmet demand to roll forward.

official_measurement_examples.name: Register not plot allocation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Entry on a self-build register records demand and does not allocate a named parcel, transfer ownership or guarantee that a suitable plot will be offered to the registrant.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning permission still required
official_measurement_examples.fact: A person on the register still needs a valid development permission for an actual self-build proposal; register membership is not planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: National data freshness guard
official_measurement_examples.fact: The latest national management-information release located in the official collection is dated 5 September 2025 for data through 2023-24; a 2026 national total must not be invented from local monitoring pages.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local monitoring context
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current 2026 local-authority monitoring can show local register demand and permissions, but those local figures must not be extrapolated as national demand or parcel-specific development capacity.

core_rules: register entry is not plot allocation
register entry is not planning permission
register demand is not parcel ownership
serviced-plot definition is not proof utilities are delivered on a named parcel
three-year authority duty is not individual delivery date
permission counted for duty must retain self-build-specific context
unmet demand rollover is not automatic parcel allocation
local monitoring is not national total
old national release is not 2026 national total
Part1 and Part2/local eligibility context must remain distinct where applicable
permission count is not completed dwelling count
register does not establish land value
register does not calculate development yield
no parcel self-build clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG/GOV.UK, legislation and current English local-authority monitoring sources checked on 2026-07-26. Register, serviced-plot, three-year duty, self-build-specific permission counting and national/local data-freshness distinctions retained; no parcel promotion.
